name: Floating pneumatic rubber fenders
description: Floating shock absorber between two vessels (STS) or vessel and quay; accommodates tidal range and ship vertical movement; soft, non-linear reaction force protects hull and jetty under overload and inclined berthing. Primary source: https://www.y-yokohama.com/global/product/mb/fenders/floating/

specifications.metric: Pneumatic 50 — guaranteed energy absorption (GEA) across standard sizes
specifications.basis: Yokohama published 'Pneumatic 50 Standard Sizes' table, from 500x1000 mm (GEA 6 kNm) to 4500x12000 mm (GEA 6473 kNm), initial internal pressure 50 kPa

specifications.metric: Pneumatic 80 — guaranteed energy absorption (GEA) across standard sizes
specifications.basis: Yokohama 'Pneumatic 80 Standard Sizes' table, from 500x1000 mm (GEA 8 kNm) to 4500x12000 mm (GEA 9037 kNm), initial internal pressure 80 kPa
Yokohama page: 'energy absorption does not decrease at inclined compression up to 15 degrees' for Yokohama Pneumatic Rubber Fenders (comparative diagrams vs solid and foam fenders)
Yokohama low-pressure table, 10 kPa initial pressure: 2500x9100 mm -> 676 kNm, reaction 1901 kN, hull pressure 88 kPa; 3300x12700 mm -> 1565 kNm, reaction 3439 kN, hull pressure 89 kPa
Yokohama explanation of ISO 17357-1:2014 new requirements, to keep metal parts safe from permanent deformation at ~80% over-compression
